messages.subject: Multinomial logit models with INLA
parts:
Hello, 

I want to model an election outcome with 11 candidates using a multinomial model in INLA. I believe this paper explains how I can do it, but here is the problem: There are some vague parts that I can't understand. 

1) In the INLA formula in page 6: 

formula = Y ~ -1 + X + W.A + W.B + W.C + 

f(phi, initial = -10, fixed = T) + 

f(alt.idx, Z, fixed = T, constr = T) 

what's the purpose of initial & fixed  terms (couldn't get it from the program catalogue) 

2) Why in the linear predictor function of the Poisson model the Gamma coefficients associated with Z should be zero sum (through constr = T)? 

3) In page 8 when explaining the "A First Random Effect" why the random effect can affect only a single category/choice? I have 11 candidates (choices) and I want city specific covariates such as unemployment to have effect on all of the choices otherwise using the structure in the paper is pointless. 

I would appreciate it if you could clarify these questions for me and let me know whether it is possible to evaluate the effect of city specific features on the winning chances of each of the election candidates using the multinomial model and INLA. 

Many thanks,

Amin

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Multinomial logit models with INLA
parts:
is the same as

f(phi, model="iid", hyper=list(prec=list(initial = -10, fixed = T)))

says that you have iid gaussian noise with precision = exp(-10), which
is a substitute for a uniform variable on the whole real ine
